title: Hesperocyparis goveniana

{{Short description|Species of conifer}} {{Speciesbox | image = Cupressusgoveniana1.jpg | image_caption = ''Hesperocyparis goveniana'' at the [[UC Botanical Garden]], Berkeley, California | status = EN | status_system = IUCN3.1 | status_ref = {{cite iucn |author=Farjon, A. |date=2013 |title=''Cupressus goveniana'' |volume=2013 |article-number=e.T42219A2962566 |doi=10.2305/IUCN.UK.2013-1.RLTS.T42219A2962566.en |access-date=13 November 2021}} | status2 = G2 | status2_system = TNC | status2_ref = {{cite web |last1=NatureServe |title=''Cupressus goveniana'' |url=https://explorer.natureserve.org/Taxon/ELEMENT_GLOBAL.2.151683/Cupressus_goveniana |access-date=8 February 2024 |location=Arlington, Virginia |date=2024}} | genus = Hesperocyparis | species = goveniana | authority = (([[George Gordon (botanist)|Gordon]]) Bartel | range_map = Cupressus goveniana range map 4.png | range_map_caption = Natural range of ''Hesperocyparis goveniana'' (''[[sensu stricto]]'') | synonyms_ref = {{cite POWO |id=60451552-2 |title=''Hesperocyparis goveniana'' (Gordon) Bartel |access-date=8 February 2024}} | synonyms = {{Collapsible list | {{Species list | Callitropsis goveniana | (Gordon) D.P.Little | Cupressus goveniana | Gordon | Cupressus aromatica | Gordon & Glend. | Cupressus attenuata | Gordon & Glend. | Cupressus barkeri | J.Dix | Cupressus bourgeaui | Gordon | Cupressus californica | Carrière | Cupressus cornuta | Carrière | Cupressus goveniana var. attenuata | (Gordon & Glend.) Carrière | Cupressus goveniana var. cornuta | (Carrière) Carrière | Cupressus goveniana subsp. gibsonensis | Silba | Cupressus goveniana var. glauca | Carrière | Cupressus goveniana var. gracilis | Carrière | Cupressus goveniana var. huberiana | Carrière | Cupressus goveniana var. parva | Lemmon | Cupressus goveniana var. pendula | A.Henry | Cupressus goveniana var. viridis | Carrière | Juniperus aromatica | Carrière | Neocupressus goveniana | (Gordon) de Laub. }} }} }} '''''Hesperocyparis goveniana''''' commonly known as '''Californian cypress'''{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17}} and '''Gowen cypress''',{{cite web |url=https://www.calflora.org/app/taxon?crn=2517 |publisher=CalFlora |title=''Cupressus goveniana'' Gordon – (not an active name) – Gowen cypress |access-date=2023-01-04}} is a species of [[conifer]] in the cypress family, [[Cupressaceae]], that is [[endemic (ecology)|endemic]] to a small area of coastal [[California]] near [[Monterey, California|Monterey]]. It was formerly classified as ''Cupressus goveniana''. ==Distribution== The tree is endemic to the [[Monterey Peninsula]] in coastal [[Monterey County, California|Monterey County]], located on the [[Central Coast of California]], in the [[Western United States]]. The tree is found in small, scattered populations, and not in large forests of its species. ''Hesperocyparis goveniana'' occurs with ''[[Hesperocyparis macrocarpa]]'' (Monterey cypress), in the two groves where the Monterey cypress occurs naturally, in Monterey County.{{cite web |last1=Hogan |first1=C. Michael |last2=Frankis |first2=Michael P. |title=Monterey Cypress (''Cupressus macrocarpa'') |website=iGoTerra.com |url=http://www.igoterra.com/artspec_information.asp?thingid=62524 |access-date=25 December 2018 |language=en}} Outside of California, ''Hesperocyparis goveniana'' has been introduced to [[Robinson Crusoe Island]] in Chile.{{Cite journal |last1=Greimler |first1=Josef |last2=Lopez |first2=Patricio |last3=Stuessy |first3=Tod F. |last4=Dirnbiick |first4=Thomas |date=July 2002 |title=The Vegetation of Robinson Crusoe Island (Isla Masatierra), Juan Fernandez Archipelago, Chile |url=https://scholarspace.manoa.hawaii.edu/server/api/core/bitstreams/605a34e5-0de7-48be-8ba2-15d69e1fffda/content |journal=Pacific Science |volume=56 |issue=3 |pages=263–284 [277] |publisher=University of Hawaiʻi Press |doi=10.1353/psc.2002.0022 |via=Scholarspace|hdl=10125/2560 |hdl-access=free }} It is on the [[IUCN Red List]] of [[endangered species]]. ==Description== ''Hesperocyparis goveniana'' is a coniferous [[shrub]] or [[tree]] with a conic to ovoid-conic crown, very variable in size, with mature trees of under {{convert|1|m|0|abbr=on}} on some sites, to {{convert|50|m|abbr=on}} tall in ideal conditions.{{cite web |url=https://ucjeps.berkeley.edu/eflora/eflora_display.php?tid=89296 |publisher=University of California, Berkeley |website=Jepson eFlora: Taxon page |title=''Hesperocyparis goveniana'' (Gordon) Bartel |access-date=2023-01-04}} The [[foliage]] grows in dense sprays, dark green to somewhat yellow-green in color. The [[leaf|leaves]] are scale-like, {{convert|2|-|5|mm|2|abbr=on}} long, and produced on rounded (not flattened) shoots. The seed [[conifer cone|cones]] are globose to oblong, {{convert|11|-|22|mm|abbr=on}} long, with 6 to 10 scales, green at first, maturing brown or gray-brown about 20–24 months after pollination. The cones remain closed for many years, only opening after the parent tree is killed in a [[wildfire]], thereby allowing the [[seed]]s to colonize the bare ground exposed by the fire. The male cones are {{convert|3|-|5|mm|abbr=on}} long, and release pollen in February/March. Typically, cones of ''H. goveniana'' are smaller than those of ''H. macrocarpa''. ===Taxonomy=== ''Hesperocyparis goveniana'' was first described and given the scientific name ''Cupressus goveniana'' by [[George Gordon (botanist)|George Gordon]] in 1849. It was described from a specimen grown in the gardens of the [[Royal Horticultural Society]] from seed collected by [[Karl Theodor Hartweg]]. It was named by Gordon for the then secretary of the society, [[James Robert Gowen]].{{cite journal |last1=Gordon |first1=George |author1-link=George Gordon (botanist) |title=New Plants, Etc., From the Society's Garden |journal=The Journal of the Horticultural Society of London |date=1849 |volume=IV |pages=295–296 |url=https://archive.org/details/journalofhorticu04hort/page/295 |access-date=8 February 2024 |location=London |language=en}} In 2009 genetic research into the relationships of ''[[Cupressus]]'' and ''[[Juniperus]]'' lead to the reclassification of almost all the new world species into a new genus, ''[[Hesperocyparis]]'' by Jim A. Bartel. This move has been disputed,{{cite journal |last1=Mаеrki |first1=Didier |title=Editorial: Recent developments in the taxonomy of the genus ''Cupressus'' and consequences for their conservation |journal=Bulletin of the Cupressus Conservation Project |date=31 January 2017 |volume=6 |issue=1 |pages=3–24 |url=http://cupressus.net/bulletin/13/BullCCP06_1.pdf |access-date=7 February 2024}} but as of 2024 [[Plants of the World Online]] (POWO), [[World Flora Online]] (WFO),{{Cite WFO |title=''Hesperocyparis goveniana'' (Gordon) Bartel |id=0000912967 |access-date=8 February 2024}} and the USDA [[Natural Resources Conservation Service]] PLANTS database (PLANTS) all list ''Hesperocyparis goveniana'' as the correct name.{{cite usda plants|symbol=HEGO3 |title=Hesperocyparis goveniana |date=8 February 2024}} The [[variety (biology)|varieties]] or [[subspecies]], formerly included under ''Cupressus goveniana'' include: *''Cupressus goveniana'' var. ''goveniana'' — reclassified as ''Hesperocyparis goveniana''. :[[Monterey County, California|Monterey County]], strictly coastal, within {{convert|3|km|abbr=on}} of the coast and below {{convert|200|m|abbr=on}} altitude. Foliage dark green, not rough, with leaf tips not spreading; cones globose. *''Cupressus goveniana'' var. ''pigmaea'', reclassified as ''[[Hesperocyparis pygmaea]]'' — Mendocino cypress (vulnerable species).[http://www.calflora.org/cgi-bin/species_query.cgi?where-taxon=Hesperocyparis+pygmaea Calflora Database: ''Hesperocyparis pygmaea''] :[[Mendocino County, California|Mendocino]] and [[Sonoma County, California|Sonoma]] counties, coastal, within {{convert|10|km|abbr=on}} of the coast and below {{convert|500|m|abbr=on}} altitude.[http://www.conifers.org/cu/Cupressus_goveniana_pigmaea.php Gymnosperm Database: ''C. goveniana'' var. ''pygmaea'' (''Hesperocyparis pygmaea'')] *''Cupressus goveniana'' var. ''abramsiana'', reclassified as ''[[Cupressus abramsiana|Hesperocyparis abramsiana]]'' — Santa Cruz cypress (endangered species).[http://www.calflora.org/cgi-bin/species_query.cgi?where-calrecnum=11186 CalFlora Database: ''Hesperocyparis abramsiana''] :[[Santa Cruz County, California|Santa Cruz]] and [[San Mateo County, California|San Mateo]] counties, in the [[Santa Cruz Mountains]] {{convert|10|-|20|km|abbr=on}} inland and at {{convert|300|-|760|m|abbr=on}} altitude. With yellow–green foliage slightly rough-textured from the acute and slightly spreading leaf tips; cones often oval.[http://www.conifers.org/cu/Cupressus_goveniana_abramsiana.php Gymnosperm Database: ''C. goveniana'' var.
